question: The diagram below illustrates the ABCE model of flower development, in which the identity structure of floral organs of eudicots is regulated by floral homeotic genes divided into ABCE-classes, based on and E-class genes stamen identity; and C- and E-class genes carpel identity. ABCE-class MADS domain transcription factors (MTFs) are key regulators of floral organ development in eudicots. Aberrant expression of these genes can result in abnormal floral traits, such as phyllody. Certain plant pathogenic bacteria could trigger phyllody in particular species, such as Petunia, which is shown in the figures below.
